newsitem.title: UK: UK to review international human rights policy.
newsitem.headline: UK to review international human rights policy.

text.p: The new British government said on Thursday it would consider signing a number of international human rights accords as part of its commitment to make human rights a central goal of its foreign policy.
Foreign Office minister Tony Lloyd told 20 human rights organisations that the government planned to launch a major review of its international human rights policy.
In particular, it would examine whether to accede to protocols to the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR) and the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR).
"Today's announcement reflects our determination to put human rights at the heart of foreign policy," Lloyd said.
"The review will look at how we can put this to practical effect by using international instruments as a means of promoting respect for human rights around the world," he added.
The ECHR protocols deal with the deportation of aliens, the death penalty and freedom of movement.

The first optional protocol of the ICCPR -- which only Britain and Greece in the European Union have yet to ratify -- allows individuals to pursue human rights cases with the United Nations Human Rights Committee, an independent expert body.
Britons already have the right to petition the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg, but the Foreign Office said the ICCPR afforded greater protection in certain areas.
